root_cause.text: The f2fs change introduced cp_enable_rwsem into the write path via f2fs_map_lock(), creating an inverted lock ordering between page locks and cp_enable_rwsem during f2fs_enable_checkpoint() remount handling, which causes a deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The reverted code added f2fs_down_read(&sbi->cp_enable_rwsem) in f2fs_map_lock() and took f2fs_down_write(&sbi->cp_enable_rwsem) in f2fs_enable_checkpoint() before sync_inodes_sb(), while the commit message shows the deadlock cycle: write_begin locks a page then waits on cp_enable_rwsem, while remount holds cp_enable_rwsem for write and sync_inode_sb/writepages then waits on the same page lock.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the cp_enable_rwsem read lock from f2fs_map_lock to fix incorrect lock acquisition in the block mapping path.
intent_record.what: The function f2fs_map_lock(struct f2fs_sb_info *sbi, struct f2fs_lock_context *lc, int flag) was modified to remove the call to f2fs_down_read(&sbi->cp_enable_rwsem); at the start of the function, leaving only the conditional locking on node_change or other locks based on flag.
intent_record.how: At runtime, f2fs_map_lock no longer acquires the cp_enable_rwsem read lock when invoked, so callers of this function will not hold that semaphore through this locking path. This changes the lock acquisition behavior and can avoid unnecessary or incorrect semaphore nesting, preventing locking-related issues such as contention or deadlock if that lock was not supposed to be taken here.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop f2fs_map_unlock() from releasing cp_enable_rwsem so it does not incorrectly drop that read semaphore during map unlock.
intent_record.what: The function f2fs_map_unlock() was modified to remove the call to f2fs_up_read(&sbi->cp_enable_rwsem); while leaving the existing conditional unlock of either sbi->node_change or the operation lock unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, f2fs_map_unlock() no longer releases the cp_enable_rwsem read lock when invoked, preventing this function from dropping that semaphore as part of its unlock path and thereby changing lock ownership/release behavior to avoid an incorrect or unintended semaphore release.

intent_record.intent_summary: Increase the default enable interval from 5 to 16 seconds so the associated enable operation runs less aggressively by default.
intent_record.what: The macro definition for DEF_ENABLE_INTERVAL was changed from 5 to 16, and its trailing comment was updated from "5 secs" to "16 secs" to match the new value.
intent_record.how: At runtime, any logic using DEF_ENABLE_INTERVAL as its default enable timing will now wait 16 seconds instead of 5 before triggering, increasing the default enable interval and reducing how frequently that enable action occurs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused or relocated `cp_enable_rwsem` lock field from `struct f2fs_sb_info` as part of internal synchronization cleanup.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the `struct f2fs_rwsem cp_enable_rwsem;` field and its accompanying comment `/* block cache/dio write */` from the `struct f2fs_sb_info` definition.
intent_record.how: At runtime, instances of `struct f2fs_sb_info` no longer contain this read-write semaphore, eliminating that per-superblock synchronization member and any direct use of it from this structure; this is a structural cleanup or part of moving/removing the related locking mechanism rather than adding new behavior in this hunk alone.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clean up f2fs_enable_checkpoint() by removing unused variables and simplifying its startup log message.
intent_record.what: The local variable declaration in f2fs_enable_checkpoint() was reduced from five long long variables (start, writeback, lock, sync_inode, end) to three (start, writeback, end), removing the unused lock and sync_inode variables. The f2fs_info() log message was also changed from a format using "%s start" with __func__ passed as an argument to a fixed literal string "f2fs_enable_checkpoint() starts, meta: %lld, node: %lld, data: %lld", eliminating the __func__ argument.
intent_record.how: This does not change the function's operational behavior; it only removes unused local variables and slightly changes the emitted log text from a generic function-name-based message to an explicit static message.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always sync inodes before enabling checkpoint and simplify this path by removing the cp_enable_rwsem lock and related instrumentation while retaining a warning for remaining unwritten data.
intent_record.what: The change removes the acquisition of sbi->cp_enable_rwsem, deletes the associated lock and sync_inode timestamp assignments, replaces a conditional call to sync_inodes_sb(sbi->sb) with an unconditional one, and updates the warning message text to a fixed string while keeping the dirty-data page count in the log.
intent_record.how: At runtime, inode synchronization is now always attempted before checking for remaining dirty data, rather than only when dirty data pages are initially detected. The function no longer takes cp_enable_rwsem in this section, so this path avoids that locking step and its removed timing instrumentation. If dirty data still remains afterward, the warning still reports it with revised wording.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove verbose checkpoint-enable diagnostic logging without changing sync behavior.
intent_record.what: A multi-line f2fs_info() logging call that printed dirty page counters for meta, imeta, node, dents, and qdata immediately before calling f2fs_sync_fs() was removed from f2fs_enable_checkpoint().
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer emits this informational log message when enabling checkpoint, but still performs the same sync operation and error handling afterward.

intent_record.intent_summary: Keep cp_enable_rwsem from being released in f2fs_enable_checkpoint() at this point and simplify the completion timing log to match the revised execution flow.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the call to f2fs_up_write(&sbi->cp_enable_rwsem); and replaces the detailed end-of-function f2fs_info() log message with a shorter message that reports only two timing values: writeback duration from start to writeback, and sync duration from writeback to end.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer releases cp_enable_rwsem at this point, changing lock-handling behavior so the write semaphore remains held past this location or is expected to be released elsewhere. It also reduces the granularity of checkpoint completion logging by dropping separate lock, sync_inode, and sync_fs timing fields.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove cp_enable_rwsem initialization from f2fs superblock setup because that semaphore is no longer needed there.
intent_record.what: The call to init_f2fs_rwsem(&sbi->cp_enable_rwsem); was removed from f2fs_fill_super(), while the surrounding lock and waitqueue initializations remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, f2fs_fill_super() no longer initializes the cp_enable_rwsem field during superblock setup. This changes initialization behavior by eliminating that specific semaphore setup, likely because the field is no longer needed or is initialized elsewhere, without adding any new checks or alternate logic in this hunk.

consistency_review.core_intent: Remove incorrect cp_enable_rwsem usage from block mapping and checkpoint-enable paths while ensuring inode sync still occurs before enabling checkpoints.
Remove the obsolete cp_enable_rwsem synchronization primitive from f2fs by deleting its struct field and its superblock initialization.
Simplify f2fs_enable_checkpoint() by removing unnecessary checkpoint-enable diagnostic logging and related unused local setup without altering behavior.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly remove cp_enable_rwsem from the block mapping/write path and checkpoint-enable path, which is the lock involved in the reported inverted ordering with page locks during remount. This aligns with fixing the deadlock root cause while preserving the required inode sync behavior.

Changing the default enable interval only alters timing/frequency of the enable operation and does not address the lock ordering inversion between page locks and cp_enable_rwsem that causes the deadlock.

The vulnerability is specifically caused by introducing and using cp_enable_rwsem in the write path, and this group removes that synchronization primitive from f2fs state and initialization. Since it directly eliminates the lock involved in the deadlock root cause, it is relevant.

The described changes only remove logging and unused local setup in f2fs_enable_checkpoint() and explicitly do not alter behavior. The vulnerability is caused by lock ordering involving cp_enable_rwsem in the write path and remount checkpoint enabling, which these cleanup changes do not address.

The group directly changes how cp_enable_rwsem is handled inside f2fs_enable_checkpoint(), which is the remount path involved in the deadlock caused by the lock-order inversion with page locks and cp_enable_rwsem. Adjusting when this semaphore is released is part of fixing that locking/execution flow.

candidates.rationale: This is the key buggy acquisition added into the block mapping/write path. It introduces cp_enable_rwsem under contexts that can already hold page locks, creating the inverted lock ordering against f2fs_enable_checkpoint().

This write-side acquisition in f2fs_enable_checkpoint() conflicts with the read-side acquisition from the mapping path, and during remount handling participates directly in the deadlock-causing lock order inversion with page locks.

This shows cp_enable_rwsem was held across the map lock critical section in the write/block mapping path. While the root cause is the acquisition, this release confirms the problematic locking scope that enabled the deadlock.

This matching release confirms cp_enable_rwsem wrapped the checkpoint-enable path. The vulnerable behavior stems from holding this semaphore in that path while it interacts with page-lock-dependent write mapping.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement introduced taking cp_enable_rwsem in the block mapping/write path via f2fs_map_lock(). Because that path can already run while holding page locks, it creates the inverted lock ordering with f2fs_enable_checkpoint(), leading directly to the deadlock described in the root cause.

Author: Chao Yu <chao@kernel.org>

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the introduced lock ordering change in `f2fs_map_lock()` and `f2fs_map_unlock()`. In `f2fs_map_lock()`, the new line `f2fs_down_read(&sbi->cp_enable_rwsem);` is taken before acquiring either `node_change` or `op` locks. In `f2fs_map_unlock()`, the corresponding `f2fs_up_read(&sbi->cp_enable_rwsem);` is released after those locks. Per the stated root cause, introducing `cp_enable_rwsem` into the write path via `f2fs_map_lock()` creates an inverted ordering between page locks and `cp_enable_rwsem` during `f2fs_enable_checkpoint()` remount handling, causing deadlock. This exact vulnerable construct is present here: `cp_enable_rwsem` is now acquired in the data/block mapping path. There is no indication in this function of any corrective handling to avoid the lock inversion; instead, this is the change that introduces it. Therefore the function contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix.
